Welcome. I’m so glad you’re here with me. Imagine a life built on strength, resilience, and a faith so steady it lights the way even when the world throws its toughest challenges at you. In a time when it’s easy to feel like your beliefs and family values are constantly under pressure, the idea of reclaiming your spiritual authority and shaping your own destiny isn’t just inspiring—it’s essential.
That’s exactly what we’re about to explore together, guided by Lisa Hawkins’ book, Christian Warrior Women: A Guide to Taking Back Your Faith, Family & Future. This isn’t just a guide; it’s an invitation to discover what happens when women step into their role as spiritual warriors—with courage, clarity, and a renewed sense of purpose.
Throughout this journey, you’ll find practical wisdom, heartfelt encouragement, and real strategies that you can use right away—whether you want to nurture your faith, protect the people you love, or create a future that feels hopeful and strong. We’ll walk through stories of triumph, biblical truths, and honest, down-to-earth advice for standing firm in what matters most.
As we move forward, you’ll feel the possibility of restoration and victory growing more real with every step. So let’s take this journey side by side—let’s reclaim what truly matters and embrace the calling of a Christian warrior woman, together.

Let’s step right into Chapter 1: Recognizing the Battle for Faith and Identity.
If you’ve ever felt powerless, overwhelmed by your daily grind, or just quietly disconnected from the vibrant faith you used to know... you’re not alone. For so many women, that sense of spiritual fatigue isn’t just a passing mood or a rough patch. More often, it’s the sign of a deeper, ongoing struggle—one that shapes how we think, relate to others, and even see ourselves.
At the center of all this is something called spiritual warfare. Now, don’t let that phrase throw you. This isn’t a clash fought with swords or shields. Instead, it’s really a battle for your beliefs, your attitudes, and the direction of your life. Maybe you’ve noticed it as persistent doubts, negative self-talk, or those patterns of discouragement that just drain your energy and hope. Sometimes, those inner battles even show up as real-life challenges—strained family relationships, tough days at work, or feeling isolated in your faith community.
Here’s something to pay attention to: understanding this dynamic is the very first step toward true change. Spiritual warfare isn’t some far-off, mysterious idea. It’s woven right into the fabric of everyday life. Realizing it’s there means seeing that faith isn’t just something you inherit—it’s something you engage with. Think of it like tending a garden. You wouldn’t just plant seeds and walk away, right? You’d guard those young plants, nurture the soil, and keep watch for anything that might harm them. In the same way, we need to protect our hearts and minds from influences that chip away at our confidence and trust in God.
And here’s where it gets personal: the core of the battle is often about identity. When criticism, disappointment, or the slow drip of lost hope shake a woman’s sense of who she is, faith can start to feel shaky too. It’s not just about what’s happening around you, but the story you tell yourself about your own worth and your place in the world.
Imagine a woman who’s spent years caring for her family. One day, she starts to feel invisible, or maybe she wonders if anything she does really matters. That nagging question—“Does my contribution count?”—starts to eat away at her, leaving her disconnected from the spiritual passion she once had. Those aren’t just feelings—they’re signs of a real battle over her identity and purpose.
So, how do you move forward when you recognize this struggle? It starts with naming what’s going on—and bringing it into the light. That means taking a good, honest look at your own heart. Maybe it’s time to admit to some feelings you’ve been pushing down—resentment, fear, or just plain inadequacy. By acknowledging the battle, you lay the foundation for true transformation.
The path to reclaiming your faith and identity begins with a few key steps:
First, pay attention to patterns—those moments of discouragement, self-doubt, or spiritual numbness. They’re clues that something deeper is going on.
Next, name the battle. Where does your faith feel shaky, or your sense of self feel threatened?
And finally, refuse to just wait for things to get better on their own. Real change asks for active engagement—it’s about stepping up, not stepping back.
This first stage isn’t about blaming yourself or replaying old regrets. Instead, it’s an invitation. What if you could see your life through a different lens—one that’s honest about the struggle, but also open to victory? When you understand what’s really at stake, you can begin to reclaim the authority and confidence that are already yours in Christ.

Chapter Two: Embracing Spiritual Authority and the Power of Choice
Now that we've recognized the reality of spiritual struggle, let's take a look at what comes next—understanding the authority that's actually available to you.
Here's the thing: spiritual authority isn't just for a select few. It's a gift, and honestly, it's a responsibility that's given to anyone who wants to live their faith on purpose—with real courage.
This kind of authority is based on the idea that you aren't just a bystander in your own life. Far from it. You're meant to be an active participant—a kind of spiritual warrior who can help shape the future of your family, your community, even your own story.
And when I say “warrior,” I don’t mean someone who's aggressive or controlling. It’s about standing strong with your convictions, making wise decisions, and refusing to let fear or resignation call the shots.
One of the biggest pieces of spiritual authority? It's the power of choice.
Every single day, you face decisions—some are small, some could change the path of your life. And these choices, they’re never made in isolation. They're shaped by what you believe, your daily habits, and honestly, the voices you let influence you.
Think about this: imagine a mom who keeps running into conflict with her teenage daughter. She might feel like shutting down or maybe even lashing out in frustration. But spiritual authority gives her another option. Instead, she can choose patience, ask for wisdom through prayer, and set healthy boundaries. By doing that, she's using her God-given authority to bring something good into the situation.
Now, let’s talk about some practical ways to exercise this kind of authority:
First, be intentional with your decisions. Ask yourself: does this choice line up with what I believe? With my values?
Second, set boundaries that protect your emotional and spiritual health. Sometimes that means saying no—to harmful patterns, or even to people who just aren’t good for you right now.
And third, speak truth—out loud, and to yourself. Instead of repeating negative or limiting stories, use your words to remind yourself and others what's really true.
It's important to remember, this isn’t about controlling people or forcing things to go your way. It’s really about taking responsibility for your own actions, your own mindset, and trusting that God can do a lot through someone who’s willing to step forward in faith.
Sometimes, spiritual authority happens in ways nobody else even sees.
It might be praying quietly for a friend, choosing forgiveness when you’d rather hold a grudge, or just holding onto hope when everything looks impossible. Those small, faithful choices—made over and over—they can honestly change the whole atmosphere of your home, your workplace, your community.
Embracing spiritual authority? It’s a journey. It takes humility, sticking with it through ups and downs, and being open to learning from both your wins and your mistakes.
When you choose to act instead of just reacting—and you root your decisions in faith, not fear—you start to reclaim a sense of agency and purpose that’s so important for spiritual growth.

Chapter Three: Healing Wounds and Restoring Relationships through Faith
So, now that we’ve built a strong foundation of self-awareness and spiritual authority, let's talk about what comes next—healing the wounds that can quietly hold us back.
If you’re like many women, you might carry scars from the past. Maybe there’s been family conflict, betrayal, or even just the slow buildup of disappointments over time. These hurts aren’t always visible, but they can create real walls—keeping you from deeper connection with God, and with the people you care about. It’s easy to slip into patterns of pulling away, mistrusting others, or feeling emotionally numb.
Here’s the thing—healing doesn’t just happen on its own. It takes real intention. You have to be willing to face the pain, but also be open to the possibility that things can get better. That’s where faith comes in, offering a way forward that’s both practical and life-changing. Instead of ignoring those wounds or pretending they don’t matter, faith encourages you to bring your pain right into the presence of God—believing that real restoration is possible.
Most of the time, the journey toward healing starts with one of the hardest steps: forgiveness.
Now, forgiveness isn’t about saying what happened was okay, or acting like you’re not hurt. It’s about making a conscious choice to let go of the grip that old wounds have on your life. It’s an act of faith that opens the door to freedom and fresh starts.
Picture a woman who’s been disappointed, again and again, in her marriage. Maybe years of unmet expectations and arguments have built up a wall of resentment. But through prayer, and some honest soul-searching, she begins to see her spouse not as an adversary, but as another person who needs grace. By choosing to forgive, she takes the first small step toward healing—not just for her marriage, but for her own heart.
Of course, restoring relationships isn’t just about the big gestures. There are practical steps you can take too:
First, create space for open, honest conversations—even when they feel uncomfortable.
Second, set healthy expectations. Real change usually takes time, and progress might be slow.
And third, don’t be afraid to reach out for support. Trusted friends, mentors, or a faith community can offer encouragement and keep you accountable.
Remember, healing isn’t a straight line. There’ll be setbacks, moments when old pain resurfaces, or when you start to doubt if things will ever change. What matters most is staying committed to the journey, and trusting that God is working, even when you can’t see it.
Community also plays a huge part in the healing process. When you’re isolated, wounds can feel even deeper. But when you connect with others—especially those who truly listen and understand—it can bring hope and perspective. Sharing your struggles with someone who gets it can break the power of shame, and open the door to real support.
In the end, the goal isn’t just to move past your pain. It’s about experiencing real, lasting restoration. That means finding joy again, rebuilding trust, and learning to love with more depth and resilience. Through faith, you can find the strength to heal, and the courage to seek reconciliation—with others, and within yourself.

Chapter 4: Reclaiming Personal Identity and Purpose in Christ
As wounds begin to heal and relationships start mending, a new question often comes up—who am I, really? For so many women, especially after a tough season or big life changes, it’s easy to feel like your sense of self has faded into the background. Family, work, and all those daily responsibilities can blur the lines between who you are and what you do. Sometimes, you might even catch yourself wondering, “Am I losing myself in all of this?”
Rediscovering your personal identity is a huge part of growing spiritually. Think of it like gently peeling back the layers of expectations, comparisons, and doubts to find the unique gifts and calling that are already inside you. Here’s something important to remember—your identity in Christ isn’t tied to your achievements, your roles, or what other people think of you. It’s rooted in the unchanging truth that you’re loved and chosen by God.
This journey—of really finding yourself again—usually starts with a little self-reflection. Taking time to think about your strengths, your passions, and even your wildest dreams can spark that sense of purpose you might’ve lost. Sometimes, it means going back to those childhood interests, exploring something new, or just giving yourself a little space to rest and let creativity breathe.
Let’s make this real for a moment. Imagine a woman who’s spent years focused on raising her children. As they grow more independent, she might find herself at a crossroads, wondering, “What comes next? Do I still matter?” When she turns to God’s guidance and listens to the quiet desires of her heart, she can start to picture a new chapter—maybe through volunteering, chasing a new career, or investing in her own growth.
So, what are some practical steps for this journey?
First, keep affirming what’s true. Remind yourself—again and again—of your worth and identity using Scripture or positive affirmations.
Second, make space for what lights you up. Even if it’s something small, carve out time for activities that bring you joy and energy.
And third, set a few goals. Pick a specific area for growth or change, and take small steps toward it. It doesn’t have to be dramatic—just steady.
Here’s a gentle reminder: don’t fall into the trap of comparing yourself to others. Everyone’s journey is different, and what fills one person’s cup might not fill yours. When you focus on your own growth instead of seeking validation from outside, you’ll start to feel more content and confident right where you are.
Identity isn’t something that stays the same forever. It shifts and grows as you move through new experiences and learn more about yourself. The key is staying open to that growth, trusting that God’s plans for you are good and purposeful.
So, by embracing your identity in Christ, you can walk into each new season with clarity, courage, and a renewed sense of direction. Isn’t that a beautiful way to move forward?

Chapter 5. Taking Practical Steps to Reclaim Faith, Family, and Future.
So, after all this talk about rediscovering who you are and why you’re here, now comes the part that really matters—turning those insights into real, everyday action.
Spiritual growth isn’t just something that happens quietly inside you; it’s meant to show up in the choices you make and the way you live your life. That’s how you begin shaping your future, one step at a time.
Reclaiming your faith, your family, and your future? That’s not just a dream—it’s something you can work toward, starting today. It all comes down to a few essential practices. Think of these as anchors that help you stay steady, even when life throws you some curveballs.
First up, make a habit of consistent prayer. Give yourself time each day to talk honestly with God—share what you’re grateful for, what worries you, and what you hope for.
Next, stay engaged with Scripture. Pick a passage that speaks to what you’re facing right now, or maybe one that inspires you to keep going. Take a few moments to reflect and let it sink in.
And don’t forget the power of community. Invest in relationships with people who share your values—folks who can encourage you, support you, and keep you accountable when things get tough.
Now, you might wonder if these routines are supposed to be strict or overwhelming. But here’s the thing—they’re not about adding pressure. These habits are tools to help you stay connected: to God, to others, and to your own sense of direction. Especially when you’re feeling stressed or uncertain, these are the things that can keep you grounded.
There’s another piece to this puzzle: being willing to step outside your comfort zone. Real growth happens when you try something new, face your fears, or make a tough decision. Maybe it’s starting a new ministry, reaching out to someone in your neighborhood, or finally chasing that dream you’ve held onto for years. Each brave step will build your confidence and open up new opportunities.
Want something practical to work with? Try making a personal action plan.
Start by identifying your priorities. What matters most to you right now?
Then, set some healthy boundaries. Protect your time and energy for the things that are truly important.
And don’t forget to celebrate along the way. Even the smallest victories are worth recognizing—they remind you that you’re moving forward, little by little.
The journey to reclaiming your faith, your family, and your future is ongoing. There’ll be ups and downs, and moments when you wonder if you’re making any progress at all. But every step forward is an act of courage and trust. Staying rooted in your faith and surrounded by people who support you will help you keep growing, healing, and leading with strength and grace.
Remember, it’s not about being perfect—it’s about making progress. You’re invited to live with intention, to welcome both the challenges and the joys, and to trust that God is working in every season of your life.
With practical steps and persistent faith, you really can reclaim your well-being, your future, and inspire those who come after you.

Chapter 6: Cultivating Spiritual Resilience in Everyday Life
Let’s dive into what it really means to build spiritual resilience—something we all need, especially when life gets stormy.
Now, if you think resilience is something people are just born with, I’ve got some good news. It’s a quality that actually grows as you practice it, kind of like strengthening a muscle at the gym. The more you use it, the stronger it gets.
At the heart of spiritual resilience is perspective. Life throws all kinds of challenges our way—sometimes it’s a sudden crisis, other times it’s that slow, relentless stress that just won’t let up. And honestly, it’s so easy to feel discouraged or even defeated in those moments.
But here’s a fresh way to look at it: what if you saw those tough moments as opportunities for growth, not just obstacles to get past? Imagine you’re a tree in a windstorm. The wind might bend your branches, but it also helps your roots grow deeper and stronger.
So, how do we actually nurture this kind of resilience? It’s simpler than you might think.
First, try a little daily reflection. Just pause for a few minutes each day and notice where you’ve sensed God’s presence—even in the tiniest ways. It’s amazing how this builds gratitude and helps you see setbacks as part of a bigger picture, not just isolated defeats.
Next, practice emotional honesty. Give yourself permission to feel everything—joy, sadness, anger, even fear—without judging yourself. When you name what you’re feeling, those emotions lose some of their power and you open the door to real healing.
And then, create some anchoring rituals. Simple routines—like lighting a candle during prayer or taking a peaceful walk at the end of your day—can quietly remind you that you’re safe and steady, even when life feels anything but.
Let me give you an example. Think about someone who’s just lost her job. Instead of letting anxiety take over, she leans into her daily rituals—maybe journaling, spending time in prayer, or reaching out to a friend who truly listens. Sure, these habits don’t magically solve all her problems, but they give her rhythm and a sense of steadiness that helps her face the unknown.
There’s also something powerful about community when it comes to resilience. When you share your burdens, ask for help, or offer encouragement to someone else, you start to build a web of support around you. It’s like having a safety net, making it easier to weather whatever comes your way.
Over time, these little practices add up. You might not notice it right away, but you’ll start to feel a quiet confidence growing inside. No matter what life throws at you, you’ll know you’re not alone—and you’ll be ready to endure.

Chapter 7—Guarding the Mind: Renewing Thought Patterns for Lasting Change.
As you start to truly grow in resilience, it’s natural for your focus to shift inward—to the world of your thoughts. I mean, let’s be honest, our minds can feel like a battlefield sometimes, can’t they? Old habits of negativity, fear, or harsh self-criticism have a way of sneaking back in, threatening all the progress you’ve made.
But here’s the thing: renewing your mind isn’t about pretending everything’s perfect or forcing yourself to only think happy thoughts. It’s about noticing when those unhelpful patterns show up, and gently choosing to respond in a new way.
Picture your mind like a garden. Every so often, weeds of doubt or discouragement will pop up. But when you tend to that garden regularly, you make room for the flowers of faith and confidence to really grow.
So, how do you actually renew your thought patterns? Let’s make it practical:
First, try practicing thought awareness. Start paying attention to the thoughts that keep coming back, especially the ones that leave you feeling anxious or ashamed. Sometimes, just writing them down can help you gain a little distance and perspective.
Next, use truth statements to gently push back against those negative beliefs. Maybe you catch yourself thinking, “I’m not enough.” What if, instead, you remind yourself, “I am loved and equipped for this moment”—drawing from your own experience, or from words that ground you.
And don’t underestimate the power of a mindful pause. When you feel overwhelmed, take a slow, deep breath and ask yourself, “Is this thought helping me, or is it holding me back?”
Let’s bring this to life with a real example. Imagine a woman who’s just had a tough conversation. Afterwards, she keeps replaying every word, starting to doubt her own worth. But then she catches herself. She pauses, names the thought, and gently reminds herself, “I am valuable, no matter what.” In that moment, she disrupts the old cycle—and lets peace in.
Over time, these small practices really start to add up. The old mental ruts of worry or self-doubt become less and less familiar, while new pathways of hope and courage take shape.
So, the big takeaway? This ongoing renewal of your mind is essential if you want to sustain your transformation and live with greater freedom.

Chapter 8: Navigating Setbacks and Embracing Grace
You know, no real journey of growth is ever a straight line. There are always going to be moments when old habits sneak back in, when your faith feels a little out of reach, or when it seems like you’re just not making any progress at all.
But here’s the thing—navigating these setbacks with a little grace? That’s a huge part of making real, lasting change.
Setbacks aren’t proof that you’ve failed. Instead, think of them as invitations—chances to gain deeper understanding about yourself. They shine a light on areas that need some extra care, and they give you the perfect opportunity to practice self-compassion.
Picture a hiker on a rocky trail. Maybe she slips, maybe she gets a little scraped up. But does she turn back? No way. She stops, takes care of her injuries, and keeps going—just a bit wiser, and much more aware of her limits.
So, what can you do when you hit those rough patches? Here are a few key strategies that really help:
First, try some gentle self-examination. When things go off track, instead of asking yourself, “What’s wrong with me?” try asking, “What can I learn from this?” That simple shift opens up so much more room for growth.
Next, don’t hesitate to reconnect with your support system. Reach out to a trusted friend, a mentor, or maybe your faith community—sometimes just a little encouragement or a new perspective can make all the difference.
And most importantly, practice grace with yourself. Remember—growth is a journey, not a finish line. Offer yourself the same kindness you’d give to a friend who’s struggling. You deserve that too.
Let’s make this real: Imagine a woman who falls back into her old pattern of saying yes to everything, leaving herself exhausted. Instead of beating herself up, she can treat this setback as a signal—a reminder to pause, reassess her boundaries, and focus on what truly matters. It’s not about blaming herself; it’s about listening and adjusting.
Embracing grace means accepting that none of us are perfect. It’s about being willing to start fresh, no matter how many times it takes. Trust that every step you take—whether it moves you forward or feels like a step back—is part of a much bigger story, one that’s held together by hope and the possibility of redemption.

Chapter 9: Sustaining Transformation—Building a Life of Ongoing Renewal
So, you’ve built resilience, you’ve started to see the power of new thought patterns, and you’ve learned to show yourself a little grace when things don’t go as planned. Now, the big question is—how do you keep this transformation going? Because real change isn’t just a single moment. It’s a series of choices, made over and over, day after day, year after year.
Think of it like tending to a garden. Some days, the sun’s shining and everything feels easy. Other days? Well, you’ve gotta put in a little extra care—maybe pull some weeds, water thirsty plants, and trust that growth is happening, even if you can’t see it right away.
Let’s talk about a few simple practices that can help you keep this sense of renewal alive:
First, try setting aside some time each month for a regular review. Just pause and reflect: How far have you come? What’s changed, even in small ways? Celebrate those moments, and don’t be afraid to tweak your goals if you need to.
Next, pay attention to the natural rhythms of your life. Productivity isn’t meant to be constant. There’ll be seasons when you need rest, times when you feel inspired and creative, and moments that call for focused effort. Let yourself move with those rhythms instead of fighting them.
And finally, think about your legacy. Every choice you make—no matter how small—shapes not just your own life, but the lives of the people around you. Maybe it’s your kids, close friends, or your community. When you keep that bigger picture in mind, it can turn even routine decisions into something meaningful.
Picture this: A woman spends a year really working on herself—building better habits, nurturing her relationships. One day, she realizes her home just feels... more peaceful. Her connections with loved ones are more honest, more real. So, she celebrates with a quiet dinner, savoring how far she’s come, and sets a few new intentions for the next season.
That’s what sustaining transformation is all about—living each day with intention, staying flexible, and holding onto hope, even when the future looks uncertain or progress is slow.
The journey goes on—and every step forward, no matter how small, is worth celebrating.

Chapter 10: Living Out Spiritual Authority—Empowering Others and Creating Lasting Impact.
Now, as we reach this final step in our journey, it’s time to look beyond just personal transformation. The real magic happens when we start empowering others. After all, spiritual authority isn’t something to keep just for ourselves—it’s really a gift meant to be shared.
Empowering others starts with simply showing up—being truly present and authentic in your relationships, your work, and your community. It’s about listening with your whole heart, offering encouragement, and modeling the kind of resilience and hope you’ve worked so hard to build.
You might wonder, how does this look in everyday life? Well, here are a few practical ways you can empower those around you:
First, mentoring. This is about guiding and supporting someone who’s just starting their own journey. Maybe you share your struggles and your small victories. Sometimes, just knowing someone’s walked this path before makes all the difference.
Then there’s creating safe spaces. Whether it’s at home, at work, or even in your church, think about fostering environments where people feel free to be honest and vulnerable. When folks know they can show up as themselves, real growth can happen.
And don’t forget advocacy—using your voice and the influence you’ve earned to stand up for those who feel unseen or powerless. Sometimes, just speaking up for someone can give them the courage to find their own voice.
Imagine a woman who’s learned to set healthy boundaries—she might help a friend navigate a tough relationship. Or maybe a mother who’s rediscovered her sense of purpose encourages her kids to chase their own passions, and to do it with confidence.
Here’s something I really want you to hear: the ripple effect of one person’s transformation can be truly profound.
As women step into their spiritual authority and start living with intention, they naturally inspire others to do the same. Over time, families change, communities shift, and even entire cultures can feel the quiet, persistent impact of people who choose to live differently.
So, what if your journey isn’t just about you? What if every step you take empowers someone else to step forward too?

As we wrap up this journey—one that’s not about following a strict formula, but about embracing a living, ever-changing process—just remember: your path will look different from anyone else’s. The heart of it all? Those core ideas—awareness, authority, healing, identity, practical action, resilience, renewed thinking, grace, growth, and empowerment. Think of them as anchors for reclaiming your faith, your family, and your future, especially when the world feels a bit out of control.
So, what can you carry with you from here? Notice and name your struggles, because that’s the very first step toward real change. Make intentional choices every day that line up with your faith and values. Open yourself to healing—sometimes that means forgiving, having honest conversations, or leaning on your community for support. Reclaim who you truly are: speak truth over yourself, explore what lights you up, and let go of the urge to compare. And don’t forget, lasting change comes from building resilience, shifting the way you think, and letting grace lead the way.
There’s no need to chase perfection here. Some days will be tough. You’ll have doubts, get tired, or feel like nothing’s changing. That’s all part of the process. Every small step—every act of courage, every fresh start—really does matter. And you’re never walking this road alone. The tools and ideas we’ve talked about? They’re meant to support you, not weigh you down. Whenever things feel cloudy, let them gently guide you back to hope.
As you head into what’s next, remember: your story’s still unfolding. Any seed of change you plant today—no matter how tiny—will bear fruit, not just for you, but for the people around you too. Give yourself permission to grow at your own pace, to rest when you need it, and to celebrate every little sign of new life along the way.
The work of reclaiming your faith, your family, and your future is deeply meaningful—and you’re more than equipped to walk it out, one step at a time.
